'''Georges-Auguste Figon''' (21 October 1926 – 17 January 1966)<ref>{{cite book|last1=Faligot|first1=Roger|last2=Krop|first2=Pascal|title=La piscine: les services secrets français, 1944-1984|date=1985|publisher=Éditions du Seuil|isbn=9782020087438|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=YlxKAQAAIAAJ&q=Georges+Figon+est+n%C3%A9+1926|language=fr|quote=Figon Georges-Auguste, né le 21 octobre 1926 à Paris (14e), Français, chimiste}}</ref> was a French chemist who was a [[Service de Documentation Extérieure et de Contre-Espionnage|freelance ''barbouze'']] (secret agent).<ref name=t19660128>{{cite news|work=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|date=28 January 1966|url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,842394-2,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105104520/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,842394-2,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 5, 2012|title=France: L'Affaire Ben Barka}}</ref> He arranged the meeting with [[Mehdi Ben Barka]] in the ''[[Brasserie Lipp]]'' in Paris. He later told ''[[L'Express (France)|L'Express]]'' that he knew who killed Barka and accused [[General Oufkir]], whom Figon had seen torturing Barka.<ref name=e20091012>{{cite news|work=L'Express |date=12 October 2009  |url=http://www.lexpress.fr/actualite/societe/histoire/chronologie-de-l-affaire-ben-barka_484113.html|title=Chronologie de l'affaire Ben Barka|language=fr}}</ref>

On 17 January 1966, before the second trial, Figon was found shot dead in his Paris apartment on Rue des Renaudes. Official records ruled death by suicide. In ''The Great Heroin Coup'' by Henrik Kruger, the author claims that Christian David shot and killed Figon.

==In popular culture==
His involvement in the kidnapping of Mehdi Ben Barka is the plot of the movie [https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0444200/ ''J'ai vu tuer Ben Barka'' (2005)].
